hook: One gigabyte of Wikipedia squeezed into 105 megabytes.

beats.say: Tufa Labs' tufazip losslessly compressed one billion bytes of Wikipedia to 105.39 megabytes, including its weights and decoder.
It took second place on Matt Mahoney's Large Text Compression Benchmark, the best entry using a neural network as its only predictor. Everything above it mixes a transformer with hand-built models.
A 163-million-parameter Transformer keeps learning while it compresses, and the decoder repeats that learning, so learned weights never ship.
